q: In the marketing-uplift-q3 project, what do we know about mq3-uplift-xl-v2?
a: An X-learner with propensity weights used for Q3 2026 targeting. It reaches uplift@20% 2.6 on the 30% split of the Q2 2026 RCT (n=330,000) and 2.2 on the Q1 2026 out-of-time set; it superseded mq3-uplift-tlearner-v1 and was shipped by dec-mq3-ship-xl.

q: In the marketing-uplift-q3 project, what came of exp-304-channel-split?
a: It measured in-app at 14.2 incremental dollars per dollar of cost, against 9.4 for email, 6.1 for push and 3.1 for direct mail. That became find-mq3-inapp-best, which find-mq3-inapp-saturates overturned: returns fall to 4.8 at three or more in-app touches, which led to the two-touch cap in dec-mq3-cap-inapp.

q: In the marketing-uplift-q3 project, what does mq3-uplift-xl-v2 depend on?
a: feat-mq3-recency-v2 (refunds excluded), feat-mq3-app-sessions-30d and feat-mq3-prior-treat, trained on the Q2 2026 RCT in ds-mq3-q2-rct, with the scoring base from ds-mq3-contacts-snap.

q: In the marketing-uplift-q3 project, which targeting model and in-app rule are in force for Q3 2026 sends?
a: The X-learner mq3-uplift-xl-v2 (dec-mq3-ship-xl, from 2026-08-04) replaces the T-learner, and in-app is capped at two touches per 14 days (dec-mq3-cap-inapp).

q: In the marketing-uplift-q3 project, what uplift@20% did mq3-uplift-xl-v2 reach on the Q2 2026 RCT split?
a: 2.6 (30% split of the Q2 2026 RCT, n=330,000), against 2.1 for the T-learner mq3-uplift-tlearner-v1.

q: In the marketing-uplift-q3 project, why did the Q3 targeting move from response scores to uplift scores?
a: A response model put 3.8% responders in its top 20%, but only $0.90 incremental spend per contact, because many of those responders would have bought anyway (find-mq3-response-trap). The uplift top 20% gave $2.40 per contact, so dec-mq3-target-uplift switched the targeting.
